entities.summary: The Nuclear Terrorism Convention is a 2005 United Nations treaty designed to criminalize acts of nuclear terrorism and to promote police and judicial cooperation to prevent, investigate and punish those acts. As of January 2024, the convention has 115 signatories and 127 state parties, including the nuclear powers China, France, India, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Most recently, Ecuador ratified the convention on January 19, 2024.
